Top-line: enterprise adtech platform (real-time personalization + reranking) evaluating Redwood Dedicated. Primary ask is firm throughput guarantees and clear burst behaviour on reserved GPUs. AE notes from commercial call and infra deep-dive.

Recent timeline:
- 2026-01-22: Intro call (Evan) — high-level ask: predictable unit economics for peak traffic, avoid noisy-neighbor throttling. Interested in 99.9% uptime SLA + latency SLOs.
- 2026-02-18: Technical deep-dive (Priya) — provided sample traffic profile (avg tokens/request 320, tails to 3k tokens). Asked Redwood for recommended GPU counts + quantization options. Recorded: ff_2026-02-18_HTRS-k9d2.
- 2026-03-03: Throughput SLA workshop (Evan, Priya, infra lead) — ran preliminary sizing; Redwood suggested baseline reserved pool of 8xA100-80GB equivalent to meet 40k tokens/sec sustained at p95 < 150ms for non-streamed responses. Recorded: ff_2026-03-03_HTRS-4b7p.

Use-case / requirements summary (short):
- Workloads: live personalization decisions (sub-100ms p50 for single-token increments), reranking of candidate lists (bursty during campaign launches), embeddings for similarity indexing (offline), chat for ops tooling (low volume).
- Latency targets: p50 40ms, p95 150ms (non-streaming); for streaming chat p95 token latency < 80ms.
- Throughput targets: sustained min tokens/sec 35k-45k depending on model variant; expected concurrency up to 1200 active sessions during peak.
- Burst policy: must support 3x sustained tokens/sec for up to 5 minutes during campaign spikes; auto-fallback to lower-cost model if sustained >10 minutes.
- Concurrency caps: prefer soft caps with queuing up to 30s, hard caps only as last resort.
- Cost sensitivity: medium — will trade some cost for guaranteed performance during US/EU peak windows.
- Data/security: VPC private deployment, SOC2/ISO required, KMS integration for field-level keys, 3-year retention controls requested in contract.

Negotiation posture / commercial notes:
- Customer requests committed baseline throughput w/ explicit tokens/sec minimum and defined burst envelope. Wants credits for each hour where p95 latency exceeds SLA threshold by >20%. Legal is pushing for a capped credit pool (they asked for 10% ARR back). Redwood's standard is 5% credit cap; AE proposing tiered credits: 1% for single short breaches, up to 5% cumulative for quarterly failures, plus technical remediation plan.
- Proposed Redwood engineering commitments: reserved pool (8 GPUs) + fast autoscale buffer (burst capacity pool) that can be triggered 3x baseline for up to 5 minutes; buffer billed at peak-rate but with reconciliation credits if used >10% of monthly burst budget.
- Customer asked for explicit concurrency-to-GPU mapping (how many concurrent sessions per A100 equiv). SE to deliver detailed model-level perf matrix and token/sec per GPU by 2026-03-17.

POC / next checkpoints:
- Perf run (synthetic replay) scheduled 2026-03-20: confirm sustained tokens/sec and p95 latency at 8 GPU baseline. Jira INF-3421 opened for custom batching knob during POC.
- Legal to return redlines by 2026-03-24 — they flagged credit language and data residency clause.
- Capacity sizing workshop w/ customer infra (30-45m) to finalize concurrency cap and burst envelope (owner: Priya).
